title: Sealed Samples for High-resolution, Microsecond Cryo-EM
content: Recent advances in microsecond time-resolved cryo-EM have enabled the visualization of dynamic biological processes on short timescales [1,2]. As described in previous works, by flash melting conventional cryo samples with a microsecond laser pulse, we keep the sample in liquid for tens of microseconds, allowing interactions with stimuli such as caged compounds, irradiation, and temperature changes [3]. However, this technique is constrained by a 30 µs observational window and a maximum temperature jump of ∼300 K, limiting access to biologically relevant timescales (hundreds of µs) and temperatures [4]. These restrictions arise from sample evaporation during laser irradiation, leading to evaporative cooling and degradation of the thin water layer. Here, we demonstrate that sealing cryo samples between thin (1.4 nm) silicon dioxide layers prevents evaporation, extending the observational window by an order of magnitude and enabling temperature jump experiments without significant loss of resolution. An overview of this process is depicted in Fig. 1.
